title: LTI 1.3 launch + QTI 3.0 export + Common Cartridge unit packs
description: Make Adaptly an LTI 1.3 tool provider so departments using Promethean / SMART / Canvas / Moodle / itslearning can launch a worksheet from inside their existing tool. Add QTI 3.0 export so any worksheet drops into any QTI-importing platform as a graded assessment. Add Common Cartridge export so a unit (the multi-worksheet bundle from Phase C · PR-5) ships as a single .imscc file.
rationale: User's improvement #7 part 3. The MAT/college tier requires standards-compliant export, not bespoke API per provider. LTI + QTI + CC are the three IMS Global standards every approved-list LMS supports.
constraints: LTI 1.3 requires JWT signing; key pair lives in env, NEVER committed.
QTI 3.0 export must validate against the IMS Global QTI 3.0 XSD (bundle the XSD, validate at build time + at export time).
Common Cartridge 1.3+ only — earlier versions not worth the surface area.
Tests use canonical IMS sample resources where available.
steps: LTI 1.3:
- Add `server/integrations/lti/` with: keyset.ts (JWKS endpoint), launch.ts (deep-link + resource-link request handling), grades.ts (Assignment & Grade Services 2.0 score posting).
- Routes: GET /lti/.well-known/jwks.json, POST /lti/launch, POST /lti/deeplink, POST /lti/grades.
- Tool config JSON for the major platforms (Canvas / Moodle / itslearning) committed to docs/integrations/lti/.
- On launch, map LTI's user_id + context_id to an Adaptly user/class via a tenant-scoped lookup table.
QTI 3.0 export:
- Create client/src/lib/exporters/qti.ts: exportWorksheetToQti(worksheet) → string (XML). Maps:
- MCQ → choiceInteraction with correctResponse
- True/False → choiceInteraction (2 options)
- Short answer → extendedTextInteraction with patternMask
- Numeric → textEntryInteraction with response-condition baseValue match
- Word-bank gap-fill → gapMatchInteraction
- Bundle assessmentSection per worksheet section. metadata.specRef + metadata.ao (from PB1) flow into qtiMetadata extensions.
- XML validated against the IMS QTI 3.0 XSD on export — failure = toast + downloadable error log.
- 'Export QTI' added to the Worksheets toolbar (next to 'Print' / 'Push to LMS') and to History row actions.
Common Cartridge:
- Create client/src/lib/exporters/commonCartridge.ts: exportUnitToCommonCartridge(unit) → Blob (.imscc). Wraps:
- One QTI assessment per worksheet in the unit
- The unit MTP + parent letter + knowledge organiser as cc-resource items
- Linked together via a top-level imsmanifest.xml with organizations + resources
- 'Export unit (.imscc)' button added to the unit pack dialog (Phase C · PC5 produces the unit).
Tests:
- server/tests/integrations/lti/launch.test.ts — verifies JWT validation against IMS canonical examples.
- client/src/lib/exporters/__tests__/qti.test.ts — round-trip a worksheet → QTI XML → validate against bundled XSD; covers each interaction kind.
- client/src/lib/exporters/__tests__/commonCartridge.test.ts — extract the .imscc, verify imsmanifest structure and resource hrefs.
Docs: docs/integrations/lti.md, docs/exporters/qti.md, docs/exporters/cc.md.
do_not_touch: LMS push routes from PC1 — LTI is a separate launch flow
Worksheet schema beyond reading metadata.ao + metadata.specRef from PB1
acceptance_criteria: Adaptly registers as an LTI 1.3 tool with a Canvas test instance and a Moodle test instance; launching from either lands on the worksheet page authenticated as the right user.
QTI 3.0 export produces XML that validates against the bundled XSD for every interaction kind covered by the worksheet schema.
Common Cartridge export imports successfully into Canvas + Moodle (manual test with a real .imscc).
Round-trip: import the QTI export back into Adaptly via a tiny QTI parser test (round-trip integrity test).
All tests pass; pnpm run check + pnpm run build pass.

size_estimate.notes: above 600 — split into PC3a (LTI launch) + PC3b (QTI export) + PC3c (Common Cartridge) for fresh chats. Each sub-PR <300 LOC.

context_budget_for_fresh_chat: MEDIUM. Read IMS Global LTI 1.3 + QTI 3.0 spec sections on first use only; the rest is template-driven.
